extracted.intended_audience: educators, school founders, and community leaders interested in industrial education and community uplift in the rural Southern Black Belt
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and principles for founding and running an industrial/normal school in a rural, agricultural region—covering educational aims, curriculum alignment with local livelihoods, funding/operation methods, student labor, and community-improvement objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational purpose of the school (practical industrial education)
rubrics_metrics.description: a school that would correct the erroneous ideas the people held of education; a school that would put most stress upon the things which the people were most likely to have to do with through life; a school that would endeavor to make education practical rather than theoretical; a school that would train men and women to be good workers, good leaders, good husbands, good wives, and finally train them to be fit citizens of the State and proper subjects for the Kingdom of God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The school should orient instruction toward practical skills and character formation appropriate to community life and civic/religious responsibilities rather than abstract theory. (Context: founding Snow Hill from an initial one-teacher, three-student log cabin.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep and develop an 'Industrial Plank' (curriculum rooted in local industry)
rubrics_metrics.description: We continued, however, to keep the 'Industrial Plank' in our platform, and year after year some industry was added until we now have fourteen industries in constant operation. Agriculture is the foremost and basic industry of the institution. We do this because we are in a farming section and ninety-five per cent of the people depend upon agriculture for a livelihood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose and expand school industries based on local economic realities (e.g., prioritize agriculture where most families farm). Build many operational industries over time rather than all at once.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start small and leverage local/community resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The Snow Hill Normal and Industrial Institute was started twenty-five years ago in an old dilapidated one-room log cabin with one teacher and three students, with no State appropriation, and without any church or society responsible for one dollar of its expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with minimal facilities and use community contributions, volunteer labor, and in-kind arrangements (examples given: house-raisings, suppers, fairs, taking wages in lumber) to erect buildings and expand programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use student labor/work-study to sustain attendance and pay costs
rubrics_metrics.description: I did not go to night school because I was given extra work ... I worked enough each month to pay my board and stay in day school. Of course, I did not have, or get any money for my work, but I did not worry about that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement a system where students perform useful tasks (maintenance, services, industrial work) to offset tuition/board costs; examples include keeping clocks regulated, making fires, maintaining electric bells, brick-burning shifts, farm work, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persist with industrial education despite local opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: When the school was started, many of the parents came to school and forbade our 'working' their children, stating as their objection that their children had been working all their lives and that they did not mean to send them to school to learn to work. ... We continued, however, to keep the 'Industrial Plank' in our platform ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect and withstand resistance from parents, illiterate preachers, and incompetent local teachers; maintain the industrial emphasis and demonstrate its value incrementally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess community conditions before and during work (reconnoitering findings as evaluation criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our trip through this section revealed the following facts: (1) That while many opportunities were denied our people, they abused many privileges; (2) that there was a colored population, in this section visited, of more than 200,000 and a school population of 85,499; (3) that the people were ignorant and superstitious; (4) that the teachers and preachers for the most part, were of the same condition; (5) that there were no public or private libraries and reading-rooms to which they had access; (6) that, strictly speaking, there were no public schools and only one private one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When surveying a region, record population and school-age demographics, school attendance and length of term, teacher/preacher literacy and competence, availability of libraries/reading-rooms, and local cultural attitudes toward education; use these as baseline metrics to plan interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black Belt Improvement Society objective (1): general uplift
rubrics_metrics.description: This society shall be known as the Black Belt Improvement Society. Its object shall be the general uplift of the people of the Black Belt of Alabama; to make them better morally, mentally, spiritually, and financially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame organizational mission broadly around moral, mental, spiritual, and financial uplift for the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black Belt Improvement Society objective (2): eliminate credit dependence & promote home food production
rubrics_metrics.description: It shall further be the object of the Black Belt Improvement Society as far as possible, to eliminate the credit system from our social fabric; to stimulate in all members the desire to raise, as far as possible, all their food supplies at home, and pay cash for whatever may be purchased at the stores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote cash-based purchasing and local self-sufficiency in food production as social/economic goals to reduce exploitative credit practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black Belt Improvement Society objective (3): cooperative purchasing
rubrics_metrics.description: To bring about a system of co-operation in the purchase of what supplies cannot be raised at home wherever it can be done to advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage cooperative buying when local production cannot meet needs, to secure better terms and reduce wasteful spending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black Belt Improvement Society objective (4): community education forum
rubrics_metrics.description: To discuss topics of interest to the communities in which the various societies may be organized, and topics relating to the general welfare of the race, and especially to farmers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use local society meetings to educate and deliberate on welfare topics, with special attention to agricultural issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black Belt Improvement Society objective (5): teach strict economy and agricultural improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: To teach the people to practice the strictest economy, and especially to obtain and diffuse such information among farmers as shall lead to the improvement and diversification of crops, in order to create in farmers a desire for homes and better home conditions, and to stimulate a love for labor in both old and young. Each local organization may offer small prizes for the cleanest and best-kept house, the best pea-patch, and the best ear of corn, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote thrift, agricultural education (crop improvement/diversification), home-ownership aspiration, and incentivize good stewardship with small local prizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black Belt Improvement Society objective (6): mutual aid fund
rubrics_metrics.description: To aid each other in sickness and in death; for this purpose a fee of ten cents will be collected from each member every month and held sacred to be used for no other purpose whatever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish small mutual-aid dues and a restricted-purpose fund to assist members with sickness and funerary costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black Belt Improvement Society objective (7): stimulate home acquisition and improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: It shall be one of the great objects of this society to stimulate its members to acquire homes, and urge those who already possess homes to improve and beautify them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage homeownership and home improvement as central goals for community stability and pride.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black Belt Improvement Society objective (8): prudent consumption
rubrics_metrics.description: To urge our members to purchase only the things that are absolutely necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote frugality and restraint in household spending to preserve resources for essential needs and long-term investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black Belt Improvement Society objective (9): combat social vices
rubrics_metrics.description: To exert our every effort to obliterate those evils which tend to destroy our character and our homes, such as intemperance, gambling, and social impurity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address moral/social problems (alcohol abuse, gambling, sexual immorality) as part of community-improvement programming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black Belt Improvement Society objective (10): civic responsibility and home beautification
rubrics_metrics.description: To refrain from spending money and time foolishly or in unprofitable ways; to take an interest in the care of our highways, in the paying of our taxes and the education of our children; to plant shade trees, repair our yard fences, and in general, as far as possible bring our home life up to the highest standard of civilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage civic duties (taxes, road care), education, and home/neighborhood beautification projects as measures of uplift and civic development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational committees for local improvement work
rubrics_metrics.description: This Society has standing committees on Government, on Education, on Business, on Housekeeping, on Labor, and on Farming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure local organizations with dedicated committees to address governance, education, economic activity, household management, labor issues, and farming; hold monthly meetings and use committees to implement objectives and discussions at the community level.
